title: Part 2.I — Scene
role: First of the four Part-2 chapters that systematically distribute the pentad terms across philosophic schools. The chapter argues that materialism is the school that features Scene as the locus of motive — environmental, material, deterministic conditions are taken as the originating ground of human action. Burke works through Hobbes (mechanistic materialism), Spinoza (the most heavily engaged interlocutor in the chapter, with the 'Alignment of Terms in Spinoza' subsection mapping Spinoza's substance/attribute/mode triad onto the pentad), Darwin (evolutionary scene), and the two great Hellenistic materialisms of Lucretius/Epicurus (atomic-swerve scene) and Stoicism (cosmic-scene). The closing 'Rhetorical and Symbolic Levels' subsection clarifies that Scene-featuring philosophies are diagnosed by which level of analysis they take as motive-locus, not by simple subject-matter. Canonical anchor for the Manual Section A entry on Scene and for the Phase 3 philosophic-school-mapping deliverable.
